title: One Sandbox, two Workspaces
blurb: Two Workspaces placed in one Sandbox with separate overlays, a slow build left to a background job, an fs write that makes a mount stale, and the refusals that keep teardown explicit: Busy, Dirty.

root.say: Two Branches, each with a Workspace: LayerFS places both in one Sandbox.

bash.description: Fork docs and site; mount both

root.note: docs and site share Sandbox 1, which has room for 16 Workspaces. The overlays are separate: site cannot see docs/guide.md.

root.say: The site build is slow. I'll leave it to a background job and keep working.
Meanwhile: a quick changelog on docs without the shell, and what teardown refuses while a build is in flight.

bash.description: Write on docs; try to unmount site

root.note: The fs write is allowed while docs is mounted, and leaves that Workspace stale. A running build still owns site's mount, so unmount waits for it.

root.say: Now I wait for the build.
The build is done. Committing docs, then unmounting both.
root.note: Commit merges the stale docs Workspace with the head, keeping CHANGELOG.md and the guide. Unmount never drops work silently: site's build output needs an explicit discard. With no Workspace left, the Sandbox closes itself two minutes later.

root.reply: docs has the guide and the changelog; site's build output was discarded on purpose. One Sandbox held both Workspaces, every teardown step was explicit, and the Sandbox closes itself once idle.
